Use\\\\n  when a patch or Windows Update install fails with 0x80073712, 0x800F0831\\\\n  (CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION), 0x800F081F, 0x800F0922, 0x80073701, 0x80070BC9,\\\\n  0x8024400A/0x80244010, or 0xC1900101; when DISM/ScanHealth reports corruption\\\\n  or \\\\\"packages are pending servicing\\\\\"; when updates stick in\\\\n  \\\\\"InstalledPendingReboot\\\\\"/\\\\\"Pending Install\\\\\"; when DataStore.edb is oversized; or\\\\n  when Windows.old lingers after a failed in-place upgrade. This skill diagnoses\\\\n  WHICH servicing fault is present and applies the correct, ordered recovery \\\\u2014\\\\n  the sub-faults interact (a stale SSU and pending transactions both surface AS\\\\n  store corruption), so the naive \\\\\"just run DISM /RestoreHealth\\\\\" loops without\\\\n  converging.\\\\nlicense: Apache-2.0\\\\nmetadata:\\\\n  version: \\\\\"1.0.0\\\\\"\\\\n  author: \\\\\"sulbri\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.agent-types: \\\\\"Chat tasks, Incident RCA\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.aws-services: \\\\\"Amazon EC2, AWS Systems Manager, AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager\\\\\"\\\\n  aws-devops-agent-skills.technical-domains: \\\\\"Windows Server, Patching\\\\\"\\\\n  domains: \\\\\"EC2, SSM, Patch Manager, Windows Update, CBS, DISM, WinSxS, SSU\\\\\"\\\\n  platforms: \\\\\"Windows\\\\\"\\\\n  supported-os: \\\\\"Windows Server 2012 R2, 2016, 2019, 2022, 2025\\\\\"\\\\n  operation-type: \\\\\"read-and-mutate\\\\\"\\\\n---\\\\n\\\\n# Recover a Windows component-servicing fault blocking patching\\\\n\\\\n## When this applies\\\\nA Windows patch / Windows Update install fails and the signature points at the\\\\ncomponent-servicing subsystem (CBS/WinSxS, servicing stack, pending\\\\ntransactions, WU datastore, or feature-update state). Instance is Online in SSM.\\\\nIf the failure is a *connectivity* fault (WSUS/TLS/proxy) or a *policy* blocker\\\\n(GPO/AV/BitLocker), this is the wrong skill \\\\u2014 those are separate domains.\\\\n\\\\n## The key insight: diagnose the sub-fault first \\\\u2014 they masquerade as each other\\\\n`0x800F0831` / \\\\\"store corruption\\\\\" is the most common *surface* symptom, but its\\\\n*cause* is often not store corruption at all:\\\\n- an **outdated servicing stack (SSU)** can\\'t process a new LCU manifest \\\\u2192 surfaces as store corruption;\\\\n- a **halted pending transaction** (interrupted reboot) \\\\u2192 surfaces as store corruption;\\\\n- a **stalled feature update** leaves mixed package state \\\\u2192 LCU \\\\\"not applicable\\\\\".\\\\n\\\\nRunning `DISM /RestoreHealth` blindly loops for hours when the real cause is a\\\\nstale SSU or a pending transaction. **Identify the sub-fault, then apply the\\\\nmatching path in the correct order.**\\\\n\\\\n## Diagnosis first (always)\\\\n- [ ] Step 1: Capture the failing error code and the servicing state before changing anything:\\\\n  ```powershell\\\\n  DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth\\\\n  DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String \\\\\"Pending\\\\\"\\\\n  Test-Path \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\servicing\\\\\\\\Packages\\\\\\\\pending.xml\\\\\"\\\\n  (Get-Item \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\SoftwareDistribution\\\\\\\\DataStore\\\\\\\\DataStore.edb\\\\\").Length/1MB\\\\n  Get-ChildItem \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\Windows.old\\\\\",\\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\`$WINDOWS.~BT\\\\\" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\\\\n  Get-Content \\\\\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\\\\\Logs\\\\\\\\CBS\\\\\\\\CBS.log\\\\\" -Tail 80 | Select-String \\\\\"ERROR|corrupt|pending|missing\\\\\"\\\\n  ```\\\\n- [ ] Step 2: Route to the sub-fault by signature (load the matching reference for exact steps):\\\\n  - Pending transactions present (`pending.xml`, \\\\\"Install Pending\\\\\", `0x800F0922`) \\\\u2192 read [pending transactions](reference/pending-transactions.md) \\\\u2014 clear these BEFORE any DISM repair.\\\\n  - SSU outdated / `0x80070BC9` / `0x80073701` on LCU \\\\u2192 read [SSU ordering](reference/ssu-ordering.md) \\\\u2014 install SSU BEFORE the LCU and before RestoreHealth.\\\\n  - Genuine CBS/WinSxS corruption (`0x80073712`, `0x800F0831` with no pending/SSU cause) \\\\u2192 read [CBS store repair](reference/cbs-store-repair.md).\\\\n  - WU datastore bloat/corruption (`0x8024400A`, `DataStore.edb` >1GB, ESENT 455/489) \\\\u2192 read [WU datastore](reference/wu-datastore.md).\\\\n  - Stalled feature update (`0xC1900101`, lingering `Windows.old`) \\\\u2192 read [feature update state](reference/feature-update.md).\\\\n\\\\n## Ordered recovery (dependencies matter \\\\u2014 do not reorder)\\\\n- [ ] Step 3: **Clear pending transactions first.** `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions`;\\\\n  rename a stale (`>24h`) `pending.xml`; clear `SessionsPending`. A pending transaction poisons every later step.\\\\n- [ ] Step 4: **Bring the servicing stack current.** Install any pending Servicing Stack Update BEFORE the LCU.\\\\n  An old SSU cannot process a new LCU manifest and will re-manifest as store corruption.\\\\n- [ ] Step 5: **Repair the component store** only after 3\\\\u20134: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`\\\\n  (add `/Source:WIM:<path>\\\\\\\\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess` on isolated fleets where WU is blocked), then `sfc /scannow`.\\\\n- [ ] Step 6: **Reset WU components** if the datastore is implicated: stop `wuauserv,cryptSvc,bits,msiserver`;\\\\n  rename `SoftwareDistribution` and `catroot2`; restart. See the datastore reference for the `DataStore.edb` specifics.\\\\n- [ ] Step 7: **Reboot** to let TrustedInstaller finalize valid pending operations, then re-scan.\\\\n\\\\n## Validation (check your own work before reporting success)\\\\nDo not report the instance patchable until you confirm each of these:\\\\n- [ ] `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth` reports the store **healthy** (not just \\\\\"RestoreHealth exit 0\\\\\").\\\\n- [ ] No packages remain \\\\\"Install Pending\\\\\"/\\\\\"Uninstall Pending\\\\\" and `pending.xml` is absent.\\\\n- [ ] No Servicing Stack Update is still pending (`Search(\\\\\"IsInstalled=0\\\\\")` returns no \\\\\"Servicing Stack\\\\\" title).\\\\n- [ ] The original failing update/patch scan re-run no longer returns its original error code.\\\\n- [ ] `wuauserv` is Running.\\\\nIf any check fails, consult the matching reference\\'s escalation section rather than re-looping DISM.\\\\n\\\\n## Gotchas\\\\n- **SSU installs are forward-only \\\\u2014 they cannot be uninstalled.** Do not promise a rollback of the servicing stack.\\\\n- **Order is load-bearing:** pending-transaction clear \\\\u2192 SSU \\\\u2192 RestoreHealth \\\\u2192 SFC \\\\u2192 reboot. SFC before a healthy store just fails; RestoreHealth before clearing a pending transaction loops.\\\\n- **A recent `pending.xml` (<24h) may be valid** \\\\u2014 renaming it can abort a legitimate in-flight servicing operation. Check age first.\\\\n- **`/Source` build must match the running OS build exactly** (`Version` + UBR); a mismatched WIM fails RestoreHealth with a generic error.\\\\n- **On an isolated/patched fleet, WU as the RestoreHealth source is blocked** \\\\u2014 supply an explicit `/Source` with `/LimitAccess` or the repair silently retries WU and times out.\\\\n- **A stalled feature update is NOT store corruption** \\\\u2014 running RestoreHealth against a half-upgraded image (\\\\\"not applicable to this image\\\\\") wastes the maintenance window; resolve the upgrade state first.\\\\n\", \"resource_manifest\": [\"SKILL.md\", \"automation/iam-policy.json\", \"reference/pending-transactions.md\", \"reference/wu-datastore.md\", \"reference/feature-update.md\", \"reference/ssu-ordering.md\", \"reference/cbs-store-repair.md\"]}'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "04b7248e-8ea2-402d-86a7-bebb3b2ea09e", "role": "user", "content": [{"id": "tooluse_BX0deyzTEd5OUZchI7vE1I", "content": "[{'text': '# Pending servicing transactions (clear BEFORE any DISM repair)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x800F0922` (CBS_E_INSTALLERS_FAILED), `0x800F081F` (CBS_E_SOURCE_MISSING),\\n`0x800F0831` with pending references; DISM \"packages are pending servicing\"; CBS.log\\n\"transaction halted\"/\"pending.xml\"; boot slow while TrustedInstaller retries.\\n\\n**Why first:** a halted transaction poisons SSU installs and RestoreHealth alike \u2014 both will\\nloop or fail until the transaction is reverted or completed.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Identify pending operations and the marker file:\\n   ```powershell\\n   DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String \"Pending\"\\n   Test-Path \"$env:SystemRoot\\\\servicing\\\\Packages\\\\pending.xml\"\\n   ```\\n2. Revert pending actions:\\n   ```powershell\\n   DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions\\n   ```\\n3. Rename `pending.xml` ONLY if stale (>24h) \u2014 a recent one may be a valid in-flight operation:\\n   ```powershell\\n   $x=\"$env:SystemRoot\\\\servicing\\\\Packages\\\\pending.xml\"\\n   if((Test-Path $x) -and (((Get-Date)-(Get-Item $x).LastWriteTime).TotalHours -gt 24)){Rename-Item $x \"$x.bak_$(Get-Date -Format yyyyMMdd)\" -Force}\\n   ```\\n4. Clear orphaned session state:\\n   ```powershell\\n   Stop-Service wuauserv,TrustedInstaller -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Remove-Item \\'HKLM:\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows\\\\CurrentVersion\\\\Component Based Servicing\\\\SessionsPending\\' -Recurse -Force -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   Start-Service TrustedInstaller -EA SilentlyContinue\\n   ```\\n5. **Reboot** \u2014 some transactions can only finalize during boot.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- Boot loop from a pending transaction \u2192 boot Safe Mode (`bcdedit /set {default} safeboot minimal`) then RevertPendingActions.\\n- Specific stuck package \u2192 `DISM /Online /Remove-Package /PackageName:<name>`.\\n- Rollback: restore the renamed `pending.xml.bak_*` if a revert removed a valid operation.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_9vlIfWdEdJrIKYRkBXovSs", "content": "[{'text': '# Servicing Stack Update (SSU) ordering (install BEFORE the LCU)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x80070BC9` (ERROR_FAIL_NOACTION_REBOOT), `0x80073701`\\n(ERROR_SXS_ASSEMBLY_MISSING) on LCU; CBS.log \"Servicing stack must be updated before this\\npackage can be installed\"; LCU downloads then fails at \"Installing\"; Server 2016 stuck on old CU.\\n\\n**Why:** the servicing stack is what *processes* update manifests. An outdated SSU cannot parse a\\nnewer LCU manifest, and the failure surfaces as store corruption \u2014 so RestoreHealth \"fixes\"\\nnothing. SSU must be current first.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Report OS build + servicing stack:\\n   ```powershell\\n   $os=Get-CimInstance Win32_OperatingSystem\\n   \"$($os.Caption) Build $($os.BuildNumber).$((Get-ItemProperty \\'HKLM:\\\\SOFTWARE\\\\Microsoft\\\\Windows NT\\\\CurrentVersion\\').UBR)\"\\n   ```\\n2. Find pending SSU vs LCU (SSU installs separately on 2016; combined on 2019+):\\n   ```powershell\\n   $s=(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateUpdateSearcher().Search(\"IsInstalled=0 and Type=\\'Software\\'\").Updates\\n   $s|?{$_.Title -match \\'Servicing Stack\\'}|%{ \"SSU: $($_.Title)\" }\\n   ```\\n3. Install the SSU first (download+install just the \"Servicing Stack\" updates via\\n   `Microsoft.Update.Session`; ResultCode 2=Succeeded, 3=SucceededWithErrors), then let the LCU proceed.\\n4. Re-evaluate the component store: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /StartComponentCleanup`.\\n5. Verify no SSU remains pending before installing the LCU.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- Server 2012 R2: download SSU from Microsoft Update Catalog, install via `wusa.exe`; SHA-2 chain may be required.\\n- Server 2016: specific LCUs require a specific SSU version \u2014 check the KB prerequisites.\\n- WSUS: ensure the SSU (not just the LCU) is approved.\\n- 2019+: ensure the combined SSU+LCU package is being offered.\\n- Since 2024, a SafeOS/WinRE update may also be required.\\n- **SSU is forward-only \u2014 it cannot be uninstalled.**\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}, {"id": "tooluse_HvbUTNS6fCysHVewe8nrTx", "content": "[{'text': '# CBS / WinSxS component store repair (only after pending + SSU are handled)\\n\\n**Signatures:** `0x80073712` (\"component store corrupted\"), `0x800F0831`\\n(CBS_E_STORE_CORRUPTION) with no pending-transaction or SSU cause, `0x800736B3`\\n(\"referenced assembly not installed\"), Error 14098; DISM ScanHealth reports corruption;\\nCBS.log \"store corruption\"/\"manifest missing\".\\n\\n**Preconditions:** pending transactions cleared, SSU current, \u22655 GB free on C:.\\n\\n## Steps\\n1. Assess: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /ScanHealth`.\\n2. Repair: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth`.\\n   - On an isolated/patched fleet WU is blocked as the repair source \u2014 supply an explicit source:\\n     `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth /Source:WIM:<path>\\\\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess`.\\n   - **`/Source` build must match the running OS build+UBR exactly** or RestoreHealth fails generically.\\n3. System files: `sfc /scannow` (only after the store is healthy \u2014 SFC uses the store to repair).\\n4. Verify: `DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth` reports **healthy**.\\n\\n## Rollback\\nRestore `SoftwareDistribution.old` / `catroot2.old` if the reset caused a regression.\\n\\n## Escalation\\n- RestoreHealth still fails \u2192 confirm WU reachability or supply `/Source`; read CBS.log for the exact missing manifest.\\n- Severe corruption \u2192 in-place upgrade repair or rebuild from AMI.\\n'}]", "status": "success", "type": "tool_result"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "516af8ab-6f41-44f8-9394-66cc8e981102", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "The core issue: blind `/RestoreHealth` loops because 0x80073712 is often a *symptom*, not the root cause. On Server 2016 specifically, the two most common hidden causes are a halted pending transaction and an outdated Servicing Stack Update (SSU) — both of which make the store "look" corrupted to ScanHealth even when the real fix is elsewhere. Here's the correct order:

**1. Diagnose first — don't repair blind**
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth
DISM /Online /Get-Packages /Format:Table | Select-String "Pending"
Test-Path "$env:SystemRoot\servicing\Packages\pending.xml"
Get-Content "$env:SystemRoot\Logs\CBS\CBS.log" -Tail 80 | Select-String "ERROR|corrupt|pending|missing"
```
This tells you whether you're actually looking at a pending transaction, a stale SSU, or genuine CBS corruption — they produce the same surface error but need different fixes.

**2. Clear pending transactions first** (if `pending.xml` exists or packages show "Pending")
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RevertPendingActions
```
Only rename `pending.xml` if it's **older than 24h** — a recent one may be a legitimate in-flight operation. Then clear orphaned session state and reboot. A halted transaction poisons every later step, including SSU installs and RestoreHealth — this is almost certainly why your two RestoreHealth runs looped.

**3. Bring the Servicing Stack Update current — before the LCU**
On Server 2016, the SSU installs separately from the cumulative update. If it's outdated, it literally cannot parse the newer LCU manifest, and that failure surfaces as "store corruption" — so RestoreHealth has nothing real to fix. Check for a pending SSU and install it first:
```powershell
$s=(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateUpdateSearcher().Search("IsInstalled=0 and Type='Software'").Updates
$s | ?{$_.Title -match 'Servicing Stack'} | %{ "SSU: $($_.Title)" }
```
Note: SSUs are forward-only and can't be uninstalled, so there's no rollback concern here — just make sure it's current before anything else.

**4. Only now repair the component store**
```powershell
DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth
sfc /scannow
```
If this is an isolated/patched fleet where WU access is blocked, RestoreHealth will silently retry WU and time out — supply an explicit source instead: `/Source:WIM:<path>\install.wim:<idx> /LimitAccess`, matching the exact OS build + UBR.

**5. Reboot**, then validate before retrying the patch:
- `CheckHealth` reports healthy (not just RestoreHealth exit 0)
- No packages left "Pending", `pending.xml` gone
- No SSU still shows `IsInstalled=0`
- Re-run the original update scan and confirm 0x80073712 doesn't reappear

Given you've already looped RestoreHealth twice without resolution, I'd bet on either a pending transaction or a stale SSU being the real blocker rather than true CBS corruption — running steps 2 and 3 before a third RestoreHealth attempt should break the loop.

If you want, I can pull the current patch state from the instance directly via SSM to confirm which sub-fault you're actually hitting.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
